I'll refine the approach to ensure accurate customer selection based on the specified country codes, account balance conditions, and order history constraints.</think>
```sql
WITH country_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT '13' AS cntrycode UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT '31' UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT '23' UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT '29' UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT '30' UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT '18' UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT '17'
),
avg_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        SUBSTR(c.c_phone, 1, 2) AS cntrycode,
        AVG(c.c_acctbal) AS avg_bal
    FROM customer c
    INNER JOIN country_codes cc ON SUBSTR(c.c_phone, 1, 2) = cc.cntrycode
    WHERE c.c_acctbal > 0
    GROUP BY SUBSTR(c.c_phone, 1, 2)
),
qualifying_customers AS (
    SELECT 
        c.c_custkey,
        SUBSTR(c.c_phone, 1, 2) AS cntrycode,
        c.c_acctbal
    FROM customer c
    INNER JOIN country_codes cc ON SUBSTR(c.c_phone, 1, 2) = cc.cntrycode
    INNER JOIN avg_balances ab ON SUBSTR(c.c_phone, 1, 2) = ab.cntrycode
    WHERE c.c_acctbal > ab.avg_bal
    AND c.c_custkey NOT IN (SELECT o.o_custkey FROM orders o)
)
SELECT 
    cntrycode,
    COUNT(*) AS numcust,
    SUM(c_acctbal) AS totacctbal
FROM qualifying_customers
GROUP BY cntrycode
ORDER BY cntrycode;
```
